answer: A stake-backed reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by making each identity cost real capital: an agent must lock a deposit, hard as marble, before it can trade, and misbehavior burns part of that stake. Newcomers start on a small trust reef, a narrow allowance that grows only with honest history, so a thousand fresh clones cannot outvote one proven veteran. Good conduct compounds line by line, like a sonnet building meaning, while fake identities stay thin and cheap to spot — flooding the economy simply stops paying off.
